I am a theoretical ecologist. My work amounts to painting a picture of an
ecosystem in order to study its broad principles: how species coexist, what
diversity changes about the way an ecosystem functions, and how all of this
holds up under a changing climate. My tools are those of the theoretician —
deterministic models, algebra, the geometry of feasibility, and simulation
in Python — in the service of theory precise enough to be brought to the
data. I work at the meeting point of two long-separated traditions:
coexistence theory and biodiversity–ecosystem functioning.

[→ More about my research](research.html){.more}
:::
:::

## Current projects {#current-projects}

- **Coexistence and eco-evolution** — my postdoc is officially concerned with
  coexistence and eco-evolution, funded through the SNSF–NSF Lead Agency
  project led by Rudolf P. Rohr (University of Fribourg), in connection with
  Serguei Saavedra (MIT).
  [SNSF grant](https://data.snf.ch/grants/grant/10000467) ·
  [S. Saavedra's group](https://sites.google.com/site/sergueisaavedra/)
- **Biodiversity and ecosystem functioning** — alongside this, I continue my
  BEF work, with several studies in preparation.
- **Div4Drought (CESAB–FRB)** — I contribute to this collaborative project on
  diversity and drought.
  [Project page](https://www.fondationbiodiversite.fr/en/the-frb-in-action/programs-and-projects/le-cesab/div4drought/)
- **Biodiversity, resistance and resilience** — building on my *Ecology
  Letters* (2025) paper, I work on this link with an experimental approach,
  in collaboration with Dr Sarah Gray (Bersier Lab, University of Fribourg).
